title: Second Opinions in Oncology - A Quantitative and Qualitative Study on Decision-Making and Utilization Processes, Barriers, and Support Needs from the Patient’s Perspective
summary:
Many people with cancer face important decisions about their treatment. A medical second opinion can help review the diagnosis and treatment recommendation and provide greater confidence in decision-making. However, little is currently known about which patients seek a second opinion, what reasons and barriers influence this decision, and what kind of support is needed.

The aim of the SO-ONC study, as part of the S.O.O.S. project funded by the German Cancer Aid (Deutsche Krebshilfe), is to investigate how often people with cancer obtain a medical second opinion and which factors influence this decision. In addition, the study examines patients’ experiences with second opinions and the support they would like to receive.

Adult patients with a cancer diagnosis will be asked to complete a one-time questionnaire about their experiences, information needs, and possible barriers to obtaining a second opinion. In addition, in-depth interviews will be conducted with a subgroup of participants. No additional medical examinations or treatments will be performed. The results are intended to help develop a patient-centered digital second opinion service and to reduce existing barriers to accessing a second opinion.

interventions.name: Adult oncological patients (≥18 years at the time of cancer diagnosis) will be surveyed or interviewed once, regardless of cancer entity and disease stage. This is a multicenter cross-sectional study using a mixed-methods design (standardized questionnaires and semi-structured interviews). Patients

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults with a cancer diagnosis (≥ 18 years old)
Confirmed cancer diagnosis (regardless of type or stage)
Sufficient German language skills to participate in surveys/interviews
Exclusion criteria:
Age at cancer diagnosis < 18 years
No cancer diagnosis
